summary: Robert Caesar Childers worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Oxford, Wadham College, and under Yātrāmulle Śrī Dhammārāma. He served as sub-librarian at the India Office (1872) and professor at University College London (~1872–1876).

Robert Chalmers specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He was educated at the City of London School and Oriel College, Oxford, and studied under Thomas William Rhys Davids. He served as president of the Royal Asiatic Society (1922–1925) and Master of Peterhouse, Cambridge (1924–1931).

Robert Chambers was an Indology scholar who studied at the Royal Grammar School and Lincoln College. At Oxford, he was Vinerian Professor of English Law (1766) and Principal of New Inn Hall (1766). He later served as Chief Justice of Bengal (~1789–1798).

Robert Charles Zaehner worked in religious studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. Educated at Christ Church, Oxford, and Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey, he worked with the SIS (~1943–1952) and served as Oxford's Professor of Eastern Religions and Ethics (1952).

Robert Cummings Neville is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Yale University (~1957–1963) and subsequently held academic posts at Yale (~1964–1965), Fordham University (~1968–1971), and Boston University (~1982).

Robert DeCaroli specializes in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his MA and PhD at UCLA, studying under Robert L. Brown and Katherine Anne Harper. He taught at UCLA and Loyola Marymount before joining George Mason University's faculty (~2002).

Robert Deliège is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Oxford (~1981–1984). He has held academic posts at the University of Kerala and as a professor at the Catholic University of Louvain (~1988).

Robert Duquenne was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He served as a specialist in Tantric Buddhism at the Hōbōgirin Institute (attested 1981) and was affiliated with the École française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 2009).

Robert E. Buswell Jr. is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied under Kusan Sunim and completed his AB, MA, and PhD at UC Berkeley. He held a professorship at UCLA (~1986–1993), later becoming Distinguished Professor Emeritus.

Robert E. Harrist Jr. is a scholar in Sinology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at Columbia University, where he is attested in 2009 and served as the Jane and Leopold Swergold Professor Emeritus of Chinese Art History (attested 2026).

Robert E. Morrell was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied under Robert H. Brower and William H. McCullough. He held an academic appointment at Washington University in St. Louis (attested in 1985 and 2006).

Robert E. Svoboda works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Oklahoma (~1970–1972) and under Aghori Vimalananda (~1975–1983). In 2008, he was an adjunct member at the Ayurvedic Institute, Bastyr University, and the Institute for Religion and Health.

Robert F. Rhodes is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who pursued doctoral studies at Harvard University. He served as a professor at Otani University (attested 1993–1997 and 2012–2014) and was a committee member for the Otani Society (attested 2000).

Robert Florida is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He served as Dean of Arts and Professor of Religion at Brandon University and later held an appointment as an Emeritus Fellow at the University of Victoria (attested 2000–2005).

Robert Ford Campany specializes in Sinology and religious studies. He served as a professor at Indiana University Bloomington (~1989–2006), worked at the University of Southern California (~2006–2010), and joined the faculty of Vanderbilt University in 2010.

Robert G. Nairn was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Zimbabwe, Edinburgh, and King's College London, under teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama. He taught at the University of Zimbabwe and was professor of law and criminology at Cape Town.

Robert Gardner studied at Harvard University (~1943–1947), worked at the Harvard Art Museums, and taught medieval art and history at the University of Puget Sound (~1951–1953). He later served as a professor at Harvard University from 1956 to 1997.

Robert Gauthiot was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1900–1907) and became a member of the Société Asiatique in 1909.

Robert Göbl was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Vienna from 1947 to 1950 and subsequently held an academic post there from around 1955 to 1989.

Robert H. Brower was a Japanologist who studied at Harvard and the University of Michigan. He held posts at Minnesota, Stanford, and the Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies, and chaired the Department of Far Eastern Languages and Literatures at Michigan (1966–1988).
